title: Notebook text at white/25-40: 23 text sites at 2.2-3.8:1 on the modal ground
body:
## Summary
Both notebook modals draw load-bearing text (fact ids, as-of dates, source names and locators, evidence citations, 'hazard not assessed', a weak engine fit) at text-white/25 to /40. On the Obsidian modal ground that is 2.2:1 to 3.8:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1. This is the same class of defect as the repo's ~0.12-alpha Ghost.

## Description
The Research step's NotebookBody and EvidenceLog modals are Obsidian world (StudioView renders <StudioFrame> with the default world='obsidian'), so they sit on .glass-panel: white 5%->1.5% over --gt-ink #080a10, about #0f1117. Effective contrast of white at alpha a over that ground: /25 2.22, /30 2.67, /35 3.21, /40 3.82, /45 4.53, /50 5.32, /55 6.21. The worst sites carry the work itself. FactRow.tsx:79 draws a source's locator, or 'no locator', at /25 (2.2:1). FactRow.tsx:89 draws the legacy `source` line at /35 (3.2:1), and that line is the only source text for every unmigrated fact row. Chips.tsx:154 draws 'hazard not assessed' at /30 (2.7:1), although HazardLine's own doc says an unasked axis must not read as clean. Apparatus.tsx:121 draws any fit other than excellent/good at /30. Argument.tsx:54/98/111/164 draw evidence citation lists at /30. Inside the bg-white/[0.02] cards the ground is lighter, so these figures are a best case.

## Flow
- Research -> open 'notebook' or 'Evidence log' -> fact rows: id, 'as of' date, source, locator, citations read as faint grey
- A low-vision reader or a bright room: 'no locator' (2.2:1) and 'hazard not assessed' (2.7:1) are effectively invisible

## Expected impact
The evidence layer, whose whole job is 'every claim dated, sourced and rated' (EvidenceLog.tsx:6-8), becomes legible at AA.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - dates, sources, locators and citations in the evidence log are readable
Before: 26 sites at text-white/(25|30|35|40) in app/_phases/_shared/**/*.tsx. 23 carry text and 3 are decorative glyphs (Apparatus.tsx:35 '→', :107 '—', Argument.tsx:144 '·'). Contrast 2.22-3.82:1
After: 23 text sites at >= text-white/55 (6.21:1) or text-slate-400. The 3 decorative glyphs marked aria-hidden and allowed. 0 text below 4.5:1
Method: probe - alpha-over-ground contrast computed with the WCAG formula. Site count by grep -oE 'text-white/(2[05]|3[05]|40)\b'
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rnoE 'text-white/(2[05]|3[05]|40)\b' app/_phases/_shared --include=*.tsx -> 26: FactRow.tsx:43,50,79,85,89; Chips.tsx:154,156; Argument.tsx:19,36,54,89,98,111,144,153,164; Apparatus.tsx:35,43,67,78,107,121; NotebookBody.tsx:115; EvidenceLog.tsx:135,143; sections/Shared.tsx:37. Ground: components/ui/tokens.ts:105 INK #080a10 + app/globals.css:161 .glass-panel; components/ui/Modal.tsx:283 (glass-panel); app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:282 (obsidian StudioFrame). Computed: /25 2.22, /30 2.67, /35 3.21, /40 3.82, /55 6.21
verify: New tests/golden-path/notebook-text-contrast.probe.spec.ts: walk app/_phases/_shared/**/*.tsx, stripComments, and collect every /text-white\/(\d+)\b/ whose alpha is < 50 on a line that does not also carry aria-hidden. Expect []. Red on HEAD (23 hits), green after. Keep hierarchy with the remaining steps (/55 for ids and dates, /65+ for source names), and keep line-through on resolved impacts as the state mark. Then photograph: CX_BASE=... node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs studio-research out.png with the notebook modal open, and open the PNG.

title: Notebook prose uses text-sm (a display rung); sibling prose uses text-content
body:
## Summary
Three paragraphs of the notebook's own prose render at text-sm (16px). Every sibling paragraph of the same role renders at text-content (18px), and globals.css says Tailwind's rungs are 'display sizes only - nothing here is a body size'.

## Description
app/globals.css:47-53: text-content (1.125rem) is 'anything the user actually READS - prose', and `--text-sm: 1rem` sits under the comment 'Tailwind's default rungs ... Display sizes only - nothing here is a body size, and the two above remain the only rungs a component should reach for'. Argument.tsx:135 (legacy counter-position prose) and :157 (typed counter-position `position`) use `text-sm`, and the steel-man statement directly above (Argument.tsx:109) uses text-content. sections/Shared.tsx:29 (CurrencyBody's `c.why`) uses `text-sm`, and the `c.advice` line two rows below (Shared.tsx:40) uses text-content. Readers see one prose voice at two sizes inside one section.

## Flow
- Notebook modal -> steel-man (18px) then counter-positions (16px). Currency: why (16px) then advice (18px)

## Expected impact
One prose size for the work's prose. The two-rung doctrine holds in the shared notebook.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the notebook's paragraphs read at one body size
Before: 3 prose sites at text-sm in app/_phases/_shared (Argument.tsx:135,157; Shared.tsx:29)
After: 0 text-sm/text-base in app/_phases/_shared. The 3 sites use text-content
Method: probe - grep -rn '\btext-sm\b' app/_phases/_shared
Result: better
Gate: none
verify: In the same probe file as the contrast ratchet: walk app/_phases/_shared/**/*.tsx, stripComments, and expect zero matches of /\btext-(sm|base)\b/. Red on HEAD (3), green after. npm run check:type stays green (text-content is a scale token).

title: Evidence log says 'See the notebook' with no control to open it
body:
## Summary
The evidence log's gaps line ends with ' See the notebook for the rest.' This is a sentence whose subject is the app's navigation. It points at a sibling modal the evidence log has no control for.

## Description
EvidenceLog.tsx:103-107 renders `{N} declared gap(s) - {first gap}` and then ' See the notebook for the rest.' (N>1) or ' See the notebook.' (N=1). EvidenceLog mounts inside its own <Modal> (ResearchStep.tsx:331-349). The notebook is a different <Modal> (ResearchStep.tsx:322-329), and EvidenceLog contains no link, button or callback to reach it. A reader has to close this dialog and find the notebook control on the step behind it. The count and the quoted gap are the work and stay. The trailing clause is the app telling the reader where to go, and CLAUDE.md's law deletes that. The surrounding comment (EvidenceLog.tsx:95-102) already says 'the notebook's own gaps section lists them all', so the clause is narration in the code's own words.

## Flow
- Research -> Evidence log -> scroll to bibliography -> 'N declared gaps - <gap>. See the notebook for the rest.' -> no control on screen to do that

## Expected impact
One fewer instruction-without-a-control. The gap count and quote stay as the work.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - copy in the evidence log is the work, not directions to another dialog
Before: 2 app-subject literals in EvidenceLog.tsx:106 ('See the notebook for the rest.', 'See the notebook.'), 0 controls to the notebook
After: 0 literals. The line reads '{N} declared gaps - {first gap}'
Method: probe - source read; grep 'See the notebook' across app -> only EvidenceLog.tsx:106
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/_shared/notebook/EvidenceLog.tsx:103-107; app/_phases/research/ResearchStep.tsx:322-349 (two separate Modals, no cross-link); grep -rn 'See the notebook' app -> 1 line
verify: Add to tests/golden-path/shared-notebook-contracts.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(read('app/_phases/_shared/notebook/EvidenceLog.tsx')) does not match /See the notebook/. Red on HEAD, green after. The gap count and researchGaps[0] stay rendered (assert the line still interpolates NOTEBOOK_COUNTS.gaps). npm run check:narration.

title: Evidence-class definitions in title={expr}: mouse-only and invisible to the gate
body:
## Summary
The six EvidenceClass definitions and the TRANSFER definition are native `title` tooltips on non-focusable spans. Keyboard, touch and most screen-reader users never get them. They are written as `title={expr}`, which check:narration's `title="literal"` regex cannot see, so the long-title ratchet has never counted them.

## Description
Chips.tsx:117 `title={interested ? `${e.why} Flagged interested: ...` : e.why}` on a <span> (EvidenceClassChip, rendered on every migrated source row via FactRow.tsx:74 and on research cards via research/_parts/CardTile.tsx:48). Chips.tsx:61 does the same for TRANSFER. Lengths: vendor 19 words, plus the 9-word 'interested' suffix = 28 words, past the 25-word hard cap the repo enforces on <Hint>. aggregator 15, self-published 15, protected 15, primary 11, TRANSFER 10. pipeline/check-narration.mjs:146 matches only /title="([^"]+)"/, so expression titles escape the budget (which reads 5/5 today). signal/README.md says native title 'does not exist on touch ... exposed inconsistently by screen readers ... unbounded'. The definitions are the work (a closed vocabulary's glossary), so the fix is a reachable channel, not deletion. A <Hint> per chip would add a tab stop on every source row, though, and that is a design call.

## Flow
- Keyboard user tabs through the evidence log -> the chips are not focusable -> the 'vendor' definition (why it is low confidence by default) is unreachable
- Touch: no hover, no definition

## Expected impact
The evidence ladder's glossary reaches every input mode, and the narration gate covers the expression form it currently misses.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an evidence-class chip's definition is reachable without a mouse
Before: 7 definitions on title={expr} (Chips.tsx:61,117), 0 counted by check:narration, 1 at 28 words (> 25 cap). 0 keyboard-reachable
After: 7 reachable (e.g. one <Hint variant="keys">-style legend per fact table, or sr-only text inside the chip), and the gate also scans title={`...`} template literals
Method: probe - word counts of EVIDENCE[*].why; regex read of check-narration.mjs:146
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/_shared/notebook/Chips.tsx:61 (TRANSFER title={...}), :83-108 (EVIDENCE.why strings), :117 (title={interested ? ... : e.why} on <span>); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/FactRow.tsx:74; app/_phases/research/_parts/CardTile.tsx:48; pipeline/check-narration.mjs:146 (matches title="literal" only); node pipeline/check-narration.mjs -> 'narration OK - 5/5 long title='
verify: (1) Widen check-narration.mjs to also measure title={`...`} template literals and title={cond ? "..." : ...} string branches. Re-run, and expect the count to rise. The director decides whether to lower the definitions or record the budget. (2) A probe asserting EvidenceClassChip exposes e.why through a non-title channel (sr-only span or Hint) - red on HEAD. (3) Photograph the evidence log after, since a glyph per row may crowd it.

title: Same rows, two names: facts/unknowns/resolved vs claims/constraints/lifted
body:
## Summary
The two notebook modals, opened from the same Research step, name the same three populations differently. The notebook says 'facts · 21', 'unknowns · N open' and 'resolved'. The evidence log says 'claims · 21', 'constraints · N' and 'lifted'. The rail fix already decided the shape (one map, two readers), and this is a pair it did not reach.

## Description
sections/H.tsx:17-38 SECTION_LABEL is the single map the rail and headings read: facts -> `facts · ${NOTEBOOK_COUNTS.facts}`, unknowns -> `unknowns · ${unknownsOpen} open`. Apparatus.tsx:68-71 marks a resolved unknown 'resolved' and :89 says 'resolved by ...'. EvidenceLog.tsx:33 tile 'claims', :49 `constraints · {open.length}` (open = the same !resolvedBy filter as unknownsOpen, notebook.ts:225), :64 `<Tally label="lifted">` for the resolved ones, and :70 `claims · {NOTEBOOK_COUNTS.facts}`. EvidenceLog.tsx:87-93 already harmonised 'bibliography' with SECTION_LABEL by hand, with a comment explaining why, so the precedent exists. Outside this context the app leans 'claims': ScriptStep's header 'N claims', RunStage 'evidence log · 19 claims', and ConstraintLedger 'this limit was lifted'. So which word wins is a vocabulary call across Research and Script, not a one-file edit.

## Flow
- Research -> notebook modal: 'FACTS · 21', 'UNKNOWNS · 2 OPEN', chip 'resolved'
- Close -> Evidence log: 'CLAIMS · 21', 'CONSTRAINTS · 2', 'LIFTED 1' - the same rows under other names

## Expected impact
A reviewer moving between the argument and the audit sees one vocabulary. The count labels stop being a second, drifting copy of SECTION_LABEL.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the same 21 rows and the same open unknowns carry one name in both Research artifacts
Before: 3 concept pairs with 2 names each across NotebookBody/Apparatus vs EvidenceLog (facts/claims, unknowns/constraints, resolved/lifted). 1 of 4 shared heads (bibliography) agrees
After: 4 of 4 shared heads read one label source (SECTION_LABEL or a renamed entry in it). 1 word per state
Method: probe - source read of H.tsx SECTION_LABEL vs EvidenceLog.tsx literals; grep of 'claims'/'lifted' usage outside the context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/_shared/notebook/sections/H.tsx:23,25 (facts, unknowns · N open); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/sections/Apparatus.tsx:70,89 ('resolved'); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/EvidenceLog.tsx:33,49,64,70 ('claims', 'constraints', 'lifted'); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/EvidenceLog.tsx:87-93 (bibliography harmonised by hand); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/notebook.ts:225 (unknownsOpen); outside: app/_phases/script/_parts/ConstraintLedger.tsx:68 ('lifted'), uat shots 05-script-adopted.text.txt:29 ('21 claims')
verify: After the director picks the word per concept: a probe in shared-notebook-contracts.probe.spec.ts asserting stripComments(EvidenceLog.tsx) builds its 'facts'/'unknowns'/'bibliography' heads from SECTION_LABEL (no literal 'constraints ·' / 'claims ·' / 'bibliography ·'), and that the resolved-state word is one constant shared with Apparatus.tsx. Red on HEAD.

lens_checked.visual-craft: all 9 .tsx in full. grep of text-white alpha sites (26) with computed contrast on the obsidian glass-panel ground. text-sm/text-content split (3). Chip tones vs Tally's CHIP_CLASS house look (Chips.tsx matches: rounded, hairline, px-1.5 py-0.5, text-label)
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: NotebookBody rail: railFor/sectionRenders agreement, jump() focus move to H tabIndex=-1, aria-current=location. EvidenceLog cross-modal reference ('See the notebook')
lens_checked.state-coverage: NOTEBOOK is a static fixture (no fetch, no failure path in the UI). CONDITIONAL_SECTIONS covers the zero-row counters/questions. EvidenceLog constraints at 0 open renders 'constraints · 0' plus a lifted Tally (acceptable). HazardLine's three states are distinct strings. useLoadFor/useStepFor: a failed read stays un-hydrated by design. usePhaseReport stamps before the write, so a failed write is not retried until deps change or remount. Checked, and a ref reset would not trigger a retry either (deps unchanged), so not filed
lens_checked.copy-auditor: SECTION_LABEL vs EvidenceLog heads. Comments read as spec (Argument.tsx:114-127 counters promise, Apparatus.tsx:97-100 questions, FactRow.tsx:54-69 sources). Notice.tsx severity doc vs signal/README UpstreamBreak severity (consistent: error rose/alert, info cyan/status)
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: Notice.tsx roles (known 2026-09-06 Lane B item, not re-filed). title={expr} on non-focusable chips. sr-only equivalents for the 'evidence ○' / 'holder ○' rings present (Argument.tsx:64-65,143-148). Rail buttons have focus-visible outlines. H headings focusable programmatically only

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: rendered inside a desktop Modal. Grids collapse via sm: breakpoints only, no narrow-first intent
